Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

Today we'll start with a new module on functional materials.

Key details

  • In that module we are going to study about polymers, the types of polymerization, structure property relationship, commercial polymers will take up butile rubber, biodegradable polymers, epoxy resin, polymer composites, cablar and carbon fiber.
  • Conducting polymers and we will look at molecular weight of polymers.
  • Then we'll also study organic LEDs.

  • A giant molecule or a macromolecule, which is formed by repeated joining of several simple molecules.
  • If you look at the picture here, we can see some small molecules over here and they have been joined together by a process which is called polymerization to give this long chain and this chain of these simple molecules is known as polymer.
  • What we have to know is between each of these small simple molecules the bond is a covalent bond now these polymer chains they could be linear they could be branched like this or they there could be a cross link network type of polymer.
  • What is a monoma then?

  • When we say simple molecule, do all simple molecules classify as small modes?
  • What is the structure of ethylene?
  • CH2, double bond, CH2.
  • What is the criteria?
  • There should be two or more binding sites.
  • Yes, we find that there are two binding sites across the double bond.
  • The double bond can open and we get two carbons wherein the bonding can happen.
  • Now here we have just one functional group, so therefore it cannot bind with several molecules.
  • It can maximum m bind with one more ovastic acid and you just end up with a dimer.

  • No, there are no binding sites at all.

  • We have COOH, and here we have CH2 four times.

  • Therefore, this also will qualify as a monomer.
  • What is styrene?
  • CH to CH and there is a benzene ring here.
  • So phenyl group, therefore, yes.
  • Where does the binding take place?
  • The moment you have unsaturation then we know that it is possible that you.
  • This double bond can open up and you have two binding sites and therefore this also qualifies as a monomer.
  • The next definition is of polymerization.
  • The process by which monomers of low molecular weight are converted to polymers of high molecular weight.
  • You can see there are double bonds, so many ethene molecules are there, and when they are polymerized, you get a chain like this and this is polyethylene.
  • One chain will be referred to as a polymer molecule.
